newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks in surprise rally end up 3.15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks in surprise rally end up 3.15 percent.

text.p: Thai stocks staged a surprise rally on Wednesday as foreign funds bought blue chip bank shares and locals invested in finance counters, analysts said.
The SET Index surged to end the day 21.90 points, or 3.15 percent, higher at 716.64. The SET 50 gained 2.14 points or 4.16 percent to close at 53.57. Turnover was 5.57 billion baht.
"This was a surprise for everyone that the market gained so much today. The only thing might be prices are cheap and discounted a lot already," said an analyst at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.
Bank stocks, headed by shares of the countries four largest commercial lenders, surged 6.15 percent. The finance sector bounced off near 1997 lows to gain 4.88 percent.
"It's amazing how the market reacted but whether this rally has legs is questionable, I think there is too much hanging over the market for that," said a fund manager at a Thai bank.

Most regional funds remained focused on Taiwan, Malaysia and Indonesia and Japanese pension funds were the only large foreign funds to have adjusted their weighting positively towards Thailand recently, he said.

"The only people overweight in Thailand at the moment are the Japanese pension funds, every other institution you can think of is underweight so it will be very interesting to see who was buying today," he said.
Some major foreign firms have recently recommended their clients accumulate blue chip bank shares arguing the stocks have discounted forthcoming bad economic news.
"There are some longer term foreign funds nibbling into the banks ... the market has discounted the bad news," said a senior analyst at a bullish foreign broker.

The bad news includes a probable Moody's Investor Services downgrade of Thailand's A2 sovereign credit rating, slowing economic growth, upward pressure on interest rates, extra provisioning and expected lower corporate earnings growth.
Bangkok Bank Plc gained eight baht to 187, Thai Farmers eight to 125 and Siam Commercial eight to 137.
